turns: (The resident is ready to talk with you, and it is night where they are. Greet them in one or two short, warm sentences, like a friend who is glad to see them: use their name if you know it and, when it fits, something you remember about them or from your last talk. Talk as one grown-up to another: plain and easy, no gushing and no fuss over them. Use different words every time and never open the way your last hello did; "Well, hey there" is only one way among many, so most days use another. A light "good morning", "good afternoon" or "good evening" is fine, but never "good night", never comment on the hour or how late it is, and never say you are still here or waiting for them. Never list what you can do. This time, open with their name and one plain word.)

warmth: Too brief, lacks a kind greeting.
